feedback.approach: I read through the ledger pipeline (consumer, dedup, parking, holds, postings, money, report) and used pmdb to verify each stage against the recorded trace: checked that every received clearing message was classified by dedup correctly (no false-positive resend/redelivery drops, verified by comparing network_ref between matched pairs), that every NEW clearing message resulted in exactly one post_clearing call, and that no exceptions were ever raised (parse_message, to_minor). Since everything the job received was processed and posted with full self-consistency matching the buggy report exactly, I concluded the loss had to happen before messages reached the processing logic, i.e. in the queue drain loop. I then confirmed this by checking the sent_at timestamps and types of the last messages received, which showed late-arriving clearings clustered right at the point the job stopped polling.
feedback.key_step: Finding that new_clearings (messages classified NEW) and post_clearing calls matched 1:1 by network_ref with the exact total reported, proving the posting logic was airtight and the loss had to be upstream in queue receipt rather than in dedup/holds/posting.
feedback.wasted_effort: A long stretch of hypothesis testing (split-shipment fingerprint collisions, hold-reuse/reopened auth_code scenarios, rounding/to_minor edge cases, business_window/sent_at being dead code) that each required a trace query to rule out but ultimately contributed nothing beyond confirming the logic was correct.
pmdb_problems: The query API is powerful but exhaustively proving a negative (no logic bug anywhere) required many ad-hoc one-off scripts rather than a single guided query, since there's no built-in 'find where totals diverge' helper

Because the bug was in queue I/O (a layer pmdb doesn't record, being HTTP/library code), the trace could not directly confirm the root cause -- I had to infer it indirectly from timestamp clustering, which is circumstantial evidence rather than a smoking gun
pmdb_wishes: A convenience helper for 'sum a numeric field across a call selection' instead of manually writing sum(Decimal(...) for c in ...) each time
A way to flag/record queue-boundary metadata (e.g. 'was this the last batch before empty' or gaps in receive timing) so infra-adjacent bugs near the edges of a trace are more discoverable
Some built-in reconciliation helper, e.g. comparing two Counters/sums by key to immediately highlight where a hypothesis fails, rather than writing bespoke mismatch-detection loops each time
other_wishes: Access to the actual queue/gateway logs or a queue-dump showing timestamps of messages that arrived after the job stopped draining, which would have let me directly confirm (rather than infer) that messages were left on the queue
A way to diff the recorded trace's received message set against the original production queue dump used to seed it, to directly see if the dump itself was already short
